args.lesson: What worked: I read diagnose.py before writing, then derived each limit claim from a boundary test against the real module, run as a library. The tests covered 50+50, 51 statements, 64+64 KiB, 65537 bytes, the shared VM budget (sized adaptively from measured ops), the per-run deadline reset and the separate modes. The edits used exact-once replacements with a reverse check, which kept the change auditable (fresh digest 473795e7...). What failed: my first test called diagnose() without query_sql. That returns INVALID_CASE without 'runs' and crashed the harness. Next time, validate the fixture shape against the function contract before you write wording. State each limit's scope (per field, per phase, per run, per mode) when it is first published, so this review cycle is not needed. Cooperative timing is supported only by code inspection.
